key_metrics.selected_arch: EX1+EX2 split (Option A) + misaligned-to-MEM (Option B) + SDC multicycle (Option D)

issues_encountered: EX stage critical path: alu_result -> misaligned detection -> trap priority chain -> ex_pc_redirect_o -> hazard unit = ~25-27 logic levels
Option C (register hazard unit) is architecturally invalid: all hazard reactions delayed 1 cycle, corrupts load-use stall and branch flush
ext_irq_i and timer_irq_i already false_path in SDC; residual constrained path from mstatus_mie_eff FF is shallow relative to bottleneck
Option A increases branch penalty from 2 to 3 cycles: +0.16 CPI (11%) at 20% branch freq, 70% taken rate
fixes_applied: Option D: add set_multicycle_path 2 from mstatus_mie_eff FF to EX stage (ISA-legal: no single-cycle IRQ delivery requirement)
Option B: move misaligned_load/store detection from EX to MEM stage; breaks alu_result -> trap_chain dependency; misalign penalty 2 -> 3 cycles (negligible CPI impact at 0.1% frequency)
Option A: split EX into EX1 (ALU compute + branch compare) and EX2 (trap priority + PC redirect); adds one pipeline stage; frequency gain ~+150 ps
Recommended order: D then B then A; combined saves ~200-230 ps, estimated fmax 540-560 MHz
notes: Architecture analysis only -- no RTL modified. This was a design-space evaluation session. Net throughput of B+D+A combination is approximately neutral vs baseline (frequency gain offsets CPI penalty). Option C must never be implemented.
